entries.0590c7d10bf56534: This is where a combination that looks surprising from the outside was born: a company making analytical instruments also makes aircraft equipment. It handles flight control systems, air management systems, cockpit display systems and engine accessories, and although its revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥43,371 million, the smallest of the 4 reportable segments, it grew 12.2% year on year, the largest growth rate, and segment profit of ¥8,220 million also grew the most, up 35.5% year on year. entries.0f009c48c10ed953: Operating income for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥73,702 million, an increase of 2.8% from the previous fiscal year. Operating income by business was ¥52,578 million for analytical and measuring instruments, ¥10,595 million for industrial machinery, ¥8,220 million for aircraft equipment, ¥4,871 million for medical systems, and ¥1,180 million for other. Few companies show such a divergence between the ranking by net sales and the ranking by profit: medical systems, second in net sales (¥73,794 million), has the smallest profit among the 4 reporting segments, and industrial machinery, third in net sales (¥71,523 million), is second in profit. Even more extreme is aircraft equipment: although its net sales of ¥43,371 million are the smallest of the 4 businesses and it has only 356 employees, its operating income of ¥8,220 million is more than 1.6 times that of medical systems, and its growth rate, up 35.5% from the previous fiscal year, was also the largest. The company explains that operating income for medical systems increased by 14.3% "due to, among other things, an improved product mix." This difference also appears in how research and development expenses are allocated: of the total of ¥23,424 million for the fiscal year ended March 2026, ¥16,410 million was allocated to analytical and measuring instruments, ¥3,025 million to medical systems, ¥1,331 million to industrial machinery, ¥419 million to aircraft equipment, ¥379 million to other businesses, and ¥1,860 million to basic research expenses and other items not allocated to any business.

entries.17d66f6eeb3ac78b: This business makes equipment for viewing the inside of the body in hospitals. It handles angiography systems, X-ray TV systems, general radiography systems, mobile ward-round systems that can be moved to patients' rooms, surgical X-ray TV systems used in operating rooms, PET systems, near-infrared optical camera systems, radiation therapy-related equipment and medical information systems. The business traces its origins to 1909, when Japan's first medical X-ray apparatus was completed. Manufacturing is carried out by Shimane Shimadzu Co., Ltd. and local subsidiaries in the United States, Germany and China, while domestic sales and maintenance services are handled by Shimadzu Medical Systems Corporation. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥73,794 million, the second largest by revenue, but segment profit of ¥4,871 million was the smallest of the four reportable segments, making this a business whose rankings differ greatly between revenue and profit. The number of employees was 1,982 (excluding 170 temporary employees). The company explains that revenue increased 1.7% year on year and operating profit increased 14.3% year on year, which is the second largest increase in profit growth rate after the Aircraft Equipment Business.

entries.48f6809998af0f26: In 1875, the first Genzo Shimadzu started, as a sole proprietorship, the business of manufacturing educational scientific instruments at Kiyamachi Nijo in Kyoto City. The securities report treats this as the company's founding. In September 1917, it was reorganized into a corporation with capital of ¥2 million, and Shimadzu Corporation was established (head office: Kiyamachi Nijo, Kyoto City). At the same time, it set up the Tokyo Branch (now a branch office), the Osaka Branch (now the Kansai Branch) and the Fukuoka Branch (now the Kyushu Branch). The head office moved in August 1919 to Kawaramachi Nijo, Nakagyo-ku, Kyoto City, and in December 1986 to the present Nishinokyo Kuwabara-cho, Nakagyo-ku, Kyoto City.

entries.4aab034bf389a082: Net sales in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥560,728 million, up 4.0% from the previous fiscal year, and the company states that it “renewed its record high.” The picture of orders is completely different from business to business. Orders in the same fiscal year were analytical and measuring instruments ¥366,517 million, industrial machinery ¥74,609 million, medical systems ¥73,975 million, aircraft equipment ¥49,181 million, others ¥5,731 million, for a total of ¥570,015 million. Order backlog at the end of the period was analytical and measuring instruments ¥115,605 million, aircraft equipment ¥89,689 million, medical systems ¥23,548 million, industrial machinery ¥17,553 million, others ¥1,828 million, for a total of ¥248,225 million. What stands out is aircraft equipment, whose order backlog of ¥89,689 million exceeds 2 times its net sales of ¥43,371 million in the same fiscal year. This is because the work takes years to deliver; orders in the fiscal year ended March 2026 decreased 14.7% from the previous fiscal year, but the portion already held amounts to 2 years' worth. Analytical and measuring instruments are the opposite: orders of ¥366,517 million are almost the same as net sales of ¥364,908 million, a business with a short period from order to delivery.

entries.4fefd2fc67b932a5: There are broadly 2 types of things it sells. The 1st is the equipment itself, and the report lists 5 businesses as “priority businesses”: liquid chromatography systems, mass spectrometry systems, gas chromatography systems, testing machines, and turbomolecular pumps. The other 1 is what is needed to keep using that equipment — consumables such as reagents, culture media and columns, and equipment maintenance services. The company calls this the “recurring business,” and in the fiscal year ended March 2026 it established a new organization to oversee the recurring business for analytical and measuring instruments. Analytical instruments are often used for more than 10 years, and consumables must continue to be purchased during that time, so the sale of 1 unit of equipment becomes the entrance to a long-lasting relationship. The same thing is happening in the industrial machinery business, and the company explains the reason operating profit increased as “due to improvement in profitability accompanying the growth of the recurring business, etc.”

entries.70525d15d0d76d1a: It is a company that brings its “measuring” technology into 4 completely different settings — laboratories, hospitals, factories and aircraft — and sells it there. The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] describes the business as “business activities covering research and development, manufacturing, sales, maintenance services, etc. in each business field of analytical and measuring instruments, medical systems, industrial machinery, aircraft equipment and others.” The pillar is analytical and measuring instruments, and net sales to external customers of ¥364,908 million in the fiscal year ended March 2026 correspond to 65% of the company's total net sales of ¥560,728 million. Its way of selling includes a mechanism that does not end with selling 1 unit of equipment. The company calls this the “recurring business,” defines it in a note to the report as “a business that provides consumables such as reagents, culture media and columns, and equipment maintenance services,” and states that in the fiscal year ended March 2026 it “established a new organization to oversee the recurring business for analytical and measuring instruments.” Because analytical instruments continue to use consumables after purchase and require periodic maintenance, a form arises in which revenue continues for longer than the price of the equipment. Sales are not to any 1 specific company, and the report states: “No information is stated because there is no customer accounting for 10% or more of net sales in the consolidated statement of income among net sales to external customers.” Net sales by region were Japan ¥242,581 million, China ¥91,736 million, other Asia ¥71,468 million, the United States ¥68,672 million, Europe ¥54,802 million, and others ¥31,467 million; Japan accounts for a little over 4-tenths, and the rest is spread across the world.

The characteristic of this business is the length of time until delivery, and the order backlog at the end of the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥89,689 million, more than 2 times the same year's net sales of ¥43,371 million. Orders received in the period were ¥49,181 million, a 14.7% decrease from the previous fiscal year.
